# benchkit

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E3 A2 H– P– · limited by scope (core), evidence (hand-computed KATs only) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — Go `testing.B` + `golang/perf` benchstat and criterion.rs, for the one comparison a maturity card quotes (ours / reference / fastest alternative, alternating rounds, cycle ratios); statistical analysis (confidence intervals, significance) is a documented gap (surveyed 2026-10-17, with `testkit`)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-29 · mutation 2026-11-14 (175/183, 3 eq) · src 8004b346081bed25

**Hardening:** fuzz n/a — parses only the output of our own foreign bench programs, never input from a consumer · ct n/a — a timing harness, no secret · panic 2026-10-29 (sweep of every pub entry point + blind review, while this was `testkit.bench`: foreign runs capped at 16 MiB of output and timed out, rounds of 0 run once, an `exes` index past the end a checked panic)

**Performance:** n/a — a timing harness: its own cost is outside the batch it times (the batch doubles past 100 ms), and nothing consumes it

**Evidence:** kat — `score`, `Summary.add`, `parseForeign`, `roundsOf`, `cyclesSince` against hand-computed rows; the capture and timeout limits against planted children (`src/root.zig` tests)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

The comparison driver behind every card `**Performance:**` line. **Bench-only**:
`build.zig` hands it to each `modules/<m>/tools/bench.zig` program (built
ReleaseFast by `zig build bench-<m>`) and to the interop tools of the modules
that list it in `interop_deps`; no downstream user imports it.

- **Platform:** any (the cycle counter is Linux `perf_event_open`; elsewhere wall time).
- **Deps:** none (std only). Its own tests use `testkit.child`.
- **Model after:** criterion and Go's `testing.B`, reduced to the comparison a maturity card quotes.

It is a module of its own, not part of `testkit`, because `testkit` is a
`test_dep` of most modules: an edit to the driver there re-keyed all of their
tests in every CI lane, while no test imports it. Here an edit re-keys the
bench programs only.

## Compared with

Surveyed 2026-10-17 as part of `testkit`'s survey (see that module's README for
the whole table).

| Project | Lang | Licence | What it has that this does not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Go `testing.B` + [golang/perf `cmd/benchstat`](https://github.com/golang/perf) — **reference** | Go | BSD-3-Clause | statistics over repeated runs (benchstat: medians, confidence intervals, significance of a delta) |
| [criterion-rs/criterion.rs](https://github.com/criterion-rs/criterion.rs) | Rust | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | warm-up, outlier classification, bootstrap confidence intervals, saved baselines and HTML reports |

**Where we are ahead:** one run times all three sides — ours, the reference
implementation, the fastest alternative — **alternating** per workload, so a
shared machine's load lands on all of them; ratios by user-mode cycles when
every side counted them; a differing output `count` between the sides fails the
run (the sides did not do the same work). Neither tool above compares against a
foreign implementation in another language in one run. **Where we are behind:**
no statistics beyond best-of-rounds and a 5 % spread flag (Backlog).

## Use

```zig
const bench = @import("benchkit");

// Per workload: ours timed in-process, the reference and the alternative as
// foreign programs printing `name \t ns/op \t cycles/op \t count`.
const summary = try bench.drive(io, arena, run, ctx, once, workloads, out);
```

`timeIt` (batch doubled past 100 ms, best of five, user-mode cycles when the
counter opens), `foreign` / `foreignArgv` (`<exe> <dir> <workload>`), `drive`
(per workload the sides alternate for `rounds`, ratios ours/ref and
ours/min(ref, alt), spread over 5 % flagged, a differing count fails the run),
`goBuild`, `buildForeign`, `foreignOnce`. `Work(Op)` carries four variations:
`info` (shown, not in the verdict), `ours_foreign` (our side timed by the
foreign program), `wall_only` (a threaded op), `fast_only` (the reference has
no such workload, so the row counts for the fastest-alternative ratio only). The scoring (`score`,
`Summary.add`) is a pure function of the rows and is what the tests check;
`example/main.zig` shows it on made-up rows.

## Verify

```
zig build test-benchkit                          # Debug
zig build test-benchkit -Doptimize=ReleaseFast   # ReleaseFast
zig build example-benchkit                       # the scoring on made-up rows
```

Provenance: original work of the zig-libs authors (MIT). No third-party source
consulted or copied, so no `NOTICE` entry is required (root
[`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE) §0). DATA: none.

## Not provided

Statistics over repeated runs (medians, confidence intervals, a significance
test for a delta, as benchstat): the verdict is best-of-rounds plus a 5 %
spread flag. The open items are under *Backlog / deferred*.

## Backlog / deferred

- Statistics over rounds (median, a confidence interval, a significance test
  for a delta, as benchstat).
- The 60 s / 600 s timeouts of `foreignArgv`, `foreignOnce`, `buildForeign` and
  `goBuild` (`run_timeout`, `build_timeout`) are constants, so no test can
  observe them: a timeout parameter (or `Run` field) a test can set to about
  300 ms would make them testable. `Cycles.open` returning null on Linux is
  indistinguishable from `perf_event_open` being denied (the documented
  wall-time fallback) and needs a lane where perf is guaranteed.
- `parseForeign` tokenizes on tabs, so empty fields are skipped: `x\t\t5\t3`
  parses as a three-field row instead of being rejected. Undocumented, unpinned.
- `timeIt` never ends on a frozen clock (not input-driven).
